desc:
An undirected graph has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1 and the edges listed in edges. A component is a maximal set of nodes that can reach each other along edges (a node with no edge is a component of its own).

A component is complete if every two different nodes inside it are joined directly by an edge. Return how many components are complete.

n = 6, edges = [[0,1],[0,2],[1,2],[3,4]]

result = 3     ({0,1,2} is complete, {3,4} is complete, {5} is complete)
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < n and a ≠ b
No pair of nodes appears twice
hints: A component with k nodes can have at most k(k-1)/2 edges, and it is complete exactly when it has that many.
Because edges never leave a component, you only need two numbers per component: its number of nodes and its number of edges.
Union all edges, then count nodes per root and edges per root (use the root of one endpoint). A root is complete when edges == nodes * (nodes - 1) / 2.
editorial: Merge the endpoints of every edge with union-find. Afterwards, group the nodes by root to get each component's node count v, and group the edges by the root of either endpoint to get its edge count e. Since there are no repeated edges, e can reach v(v-1)/2 only when every pair of nodes is joined, so a component is complete exactly when e == v(v-1)/2.

Isolated nodes have v = 1 and e = 0, which satisfies the formula, so they count as complete. Time is O(n + m · α(n)). This pattern, collecting a statistic per union-find root after all unions, is very common in component problems.
